  scale_size_area(max_size=15) +

You can normalize the y values within the x groups and use these to assign colors. The numbers in the legend become meaningless, though, and you’ll want to modify or get rid of it:
require(ggplot2)
require(plyr)
set.seed(1)
df <- data.frame(x=c(rep("a", 10), rep("b", 10)),
                 y=c(sample(1:4, 10, replace=T), sample(1:6, 10, replace=T)))
df <- ddply(df, .(x), transform, y2=(y-min(y))/(max(y)-min(y)))  # <--- Normalized y values are "y2"
ggplot(data=df, aes(x=x, y=y)) +
  stat_sum(aes(group=x, color=y2)) +        # <---  Assign color to "y2"
  scale_size_area(max_size=15) +
  scale_color_gradient(low="red", high="green", breaks=c(0,1),  # <--- Modify the scale labels
                       label=c("min.group", "max.group"))

messages.body_plain:
Hi All

I want to conditional replace the values of a vector (df$var2) based on values of df$var1. Usually, I would write that as

df$var2 [df$var1 == "x"] <- df$var3 [df$var1 == "x"]

However, the above code looks at the value of var1 in the same row. I want to look either at a latter row or a prior row. Which row is again conditional. Which functions should I look at?

Specifically, in the attached excel, where var2 gives the travel purpose of a travel, and var1 identifies a location as an "anchor" location or not.
Travel1 (Activity #4) is a home to office trip, hence travel purpose (var2) is based on activity in office (var3, "work").
Similarly Travel2 (Activity#6) is a travel to work.
In contrast, Travel3 (Activity#10) depends upon prior value of var2 because the destination location is Home. Hence the travel purpose is based on activity in the prior anchor location (work in office).

messages.subject_clean: [D-RUG]: Conditional replacement of values in a data.frame
messages.body_plain:
Tricky! To clarify, I think the problem is the following:

TravelPurpose should be “Work” IF
The LAST location which is an anchor location is “Office” OR
The Previous location which is an anchor location is “Office”

This seems like a good place to break out the old for loop, as each iteration depends on values before and after it. There may be a more elegant vectorized solution, but this works:
# Load data and empty var1. Make sure to encode strings as characters, factors
# will mess up the logic below
df = read.csv("DRUGJul2.csv", stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
df$var1=character(11)

# Create vectors with the indices of anchor locations and travel activities
anchors = which(df$var2==1)
travels = which(df$var3=="Travel")

#Iterate through "travel" locations
for(i in travels) {
  last_anchor = df$location[max(anchors[anchors < i])]  #Get last anchor loc
  next_anchor = df$location[min(anchors[anchors > i])]  #Get next anchor loc
  if("Office" %in% c(last_anchor, next_anchor)) {       #Are either "Office"?
    df$var1[i] = "Work"
  }
}

You’ll get warnings if you have “Travel” values in the first and last rows but it should still work.

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

This is my first reply in this group :)

Working with the code and object you provided. Here is how you should be able to dynamically set the label colors:

mydata<-read.csv("Plant Comm Year 2 N Plots.csv", header=TRUE,row.names=1)
library(vegan)
mydata <- decostand(mydata, method = "total")
# check total abundance in each sample
apply(mydata, 1, sum)
# look at the transformed data
mydata[1:5, 1:5]
ls()
# calculate Bray-Curtis distance among samples
mydata.bc.dist <- vegdist(mydata, method = "bray")
# cluster communities using average-linkage algorithm
mydata.bc.clust <- hclust(mydata.bc.dist, method = "average")
# plot cluster diagram
plot(mydata.bc.clust, ylab = "Bray-Curtis dissimilarity",col=rainbow(3))

#-------------Additions-------------------
#define colors you would like
# best way to do this is starting from a column giving the treatments
treat<-c(rep(1,10),rep(2,10),rep(3,10),rep(4,10))
# set colors
mycolors<-c("blue","purple","orange","red")[factor(treat)] # using factor to subset is useful when treatments are out of order

## function to set label color
# see added color.key which you can define for your data
labelCol <- function(x,color.key) {
  if (is.leaf(x)) {
    ## fetch label
    label <- attr(x, "label")
    ## set label color
color<-unname(color.key[label,])
    attr(x, "nodePar") <- list(lab.col=color)
  }
  return(x)
}

## apply labelCol on all nodes of the dendrogram
color.key<-matrix(mycolors);rownames(color.key)<-rownames(mydata) # extraction is done on rownames,use make.unique() if not unique
d <- dendrapply(as.dendrogram(mydata.bc.clust), labelCol, color.key)

plot(d)

#------------end

Hope this helps.
-Dmitry

messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I am having trouble getting percent on the y-axis of a ggplot stacked histogram from a grouped dataframe. Normally, `y = (..count..)/sum(..count..)`
accomplishes this, but with the grouped dataframe, `sum(..count..)` seems to be summing the ungrouped entries. Note the y-axis:

require(ggplot)
require(dplyr)
set.seed(95616)
df <- data.frame(group1=rep(letters[1:10], each=5),
                 question=rep(1:5),
                 answer=sample(1:4, 50, replace=T))

df %>%
  group_by(group1, question) %>%
  summarise(response = median(answer)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = question,
             y = (..count..)/sum(..count..),
             fill=as.factor(response))) +
  geom_bar() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format())

To get the proper percentages, I need to divide the counts by the number of groups, which is `nlevels(df$group1)`, 10. Using `y = (..count..)/10` works, but I want to do it programmatically and can't. I've tried a bunch of ways <http://stackoverflow.com/questions/10659133/local-variables-within-aes> (below) to bring `nlevels(df$group1)` into the y aes expression, and all fail. Any ideas?

df %>%
  group_by(group1, question) %>%
  summarise(response = median(answer)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = question,
             y = (..count..)/nlevels(group1),
             fill=as.factor(response))) +
  geom_bar() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format())

df <- cbind(df, n.levels=nlevels(df$group1))
df %>%
  group_by(group1, question) %>%
  summarise(response = median(answer)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = question,
             y = (..count..)/n.levels[1],
             fill=as.factor(response))) +
  geom_bar() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format())

.e <- environment()
df %>%
  group_by(group1, question) %>%
  summarise(response = median(answer)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = question,
             y = (..count..)/n.levels,
             fill=as.factor(response)),
         environment = .e) +
  geom_bar() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format())

n.levels <- nlevels(df$group1)
df %>%
  group_by(group1, question) %>%
  summarise(response = median(answer)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = question,
             y = (..count..)/n.levels,
             fill=as.factor(response)),
         environment = environment()) +
  geom_bar() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format())

messages.body_plain:
Dear R users;

I have a data frame kind of like this one, in which there is a grouping variable and a variable containing the data of interest.  The row names are not the same as the row indices.

df <-
  data.frame(groupVar=c(1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 4),
                     Var1=c(8.2, 3.4, 6.1, 7.5, 2.9, 0.7, 4.6, 5.5, 3.2, 9.1),
                     row.names=c(111, 135, 178, 264, 279, 295, 342, 370, 381, 421))

Right now I am only interested in the observations of Var1 that are not the maximum of their group, so I made a vector of the row indices with observations that are not the group maximum.

not.max.rows <-
  unlist(sapply(unique(df$groupVar),
                       function(x)
                          {which(df$groupVar==x &
                                        df$Var1!=max(df$Var1[which(df$groupVar==x)]))}))

Now I would like to be able to access the values of Var1 within a specified group that are not the maximum of the group.  So, I tried combined indexing by my vector of row indices that are not the group maximum and a which() statement specifying the group I want, but it did not work.

df$Var1[not.max.rows][which(df$groupVar==2)]

It would sure be convenient to be able to index by a which() statement and row indices at the same time.  Is there a way to do this?  If not, I guess I could index by a vector of row names, rather than row indices, but is there a simpler way of doing this that I have missed?

Bonnie

messages.body_plain:
Hi D-RUG folks.

I have a data manipulation task that a I have a way of doing, but I would like to be able to do it with dplyr, if possible, and I am currently stumped.

I have a data frame of all the nights of sleep (or naps) recorded by five people, including the date and the sleep duration in hours.

require(lubridate)

require(dplyr)

nights.all <-

  data.frame(person.id <http://person.id> = c(1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 4, 5, 5, 5, 5),

             record.date = ymd("2009-09-17", "2009-09-18", "2009-09-20", "2010-02-23",

                                "2010-03-01", "2009-07-03", "2009-07-03", "2009-07-04",

                                "2009-07-05", "2009-07-07", "2011-11-30", "2010-04-16",

                                "2010-04-17", "2010-04-18", "2010-04-21"),

             sleep = c(8.2, 7.1, NA, 5.4, 6.7, 0.6, 7.2, 6.8, 7.5, 6.8, NA, 6.1, 6.2, NA, 7.3))

I extracted the rows that meet criteria for an analysis I want to do into a different data frame, called nights.

nights <- nights.all[c(1, 2, 4, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12, 14, 15), ]

I would like to add a column to the nights data frame containing, for each row, the total amount of sleep obtained on the prior date, if available.  Here is how I am currently doing this:

nights.list <- split(nights, nights$person.id <http://person.id>)

nights.all.list <- split(nights.all, nights.all$person.id <http://person.id>)

prior.sleep <-

  mapply(function(x, y)

           {sapply(x$record.date,

                   function(z)

                     {ifelse(length(which(!is.na <http://is.na>(y$sleep[

                               which(y$record.date == z - days(1))]))) > 0,

                             sum(y$sleep[which(y$record.date == z - days(1))],

                                 na.rm=T),

                             NA)})},

         nights.list, nights.all.list)

nights$prior.sleep <- unlist(prior.sleep)

Can anyone suggest a way to do this using dplyr instead?

Thanks.

Bonnie

Are there duplicated observations per person per day? e.g. two separate entries for the same person on the same day? This doesn't seem to the case in your test data, and makes life easier. Here's a quick test:

Vince
